question: For the system $kx+2y=4$ and $2x+ky=4$, determine the number of solutions for $k\ne\pm2$, $k=2$ and $k=-2$. Give reasons for each case.
explanation:
Coefficient determinant
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is $$\begin{vmatrix}k&2\\2&k\end{vmatrix}=k^2-4=(k-2)(k+2)$$
Case $k\ne\pm2$
The determinant is nonzero, so the system has a unique solution.
Case $k=2$
The equations become $2x+2y=4$ and $2x+2y=4$. They are identical, so the system has infinitely many solutions.
Case $k=-2$
The equations become $-2x+2y=4$ and $2x-2y=4$. Multiplying the first equation by $-1$ gives $2x-2y=-4$, which contradicts the second equation. Hence, there is no solution.
Thus, the three cases give one, infinitely many and zero solutions, respectively.

options.A: For $k\ne\pm2$: infinitely many solutions; $k=2$: unique solution; $k=-2$: no solution.
options.B: For $k\ne\pm2$: unique solution; $k=2$: infinitely many solutions; $k=-2$: no solution.
options.C: For $k\ne\pm2$: unique solution; $k=2$: no solution; $k=-2$: infinitely many solutions.
options.D: For $k\ne\pm2$: no solution; $k=2$: infinitely many solutions; $k=-2$: unique solution.
